alignments.note: Rule 14: the waw of וְעַתָּה takes the connective the ASV wrote for it, here *therefore*, which the corpus lists among a waw's renderings. Competing reading: give *now therefore* whole to עַתָּה and mark the waw unrepresented; taken this way because a written connective is never left to a neighbouring word.
The temporal adverb takes *now*.
Imperative לְךָ → *Come*.
Rule 32: the emphatic/cohortative he (tag Sh, not Sd) has no English realization.
Rule 30's closing sentence: the entreaty particle נָא takes the complete formula *I pray thee*, headed on *pray*; its pronouns are not added.
Imperative אָרָה → *curse*.
Rule 32: emphatic he on אָרָה, no English.
Rule 40: the dative לְ rendered as a bare English indirect object (*curse me*) keeps no word of its own.
Rule 40: the suffix takes the pronoun *me*.
Rule 16: the object marker is unrendered; the ASV writes the object bare.
Rule 41: the ASV writes one determiner for the phrase, *this*, which the demonstrative pronoun licenses; the noun's article is left with nothing.
עָם → *people*.
Rule 47: the agreement article on the demonstrative is unrepresented, the phrase's single determiner having gone to הַזֶּה.
Rule 41: a demonstrative pronoun standing in the phrase is what the written *this* renders.
כִּי → *for*.
Rule 20: the verbless clause's supplied copula joins the predicate adjective, and the comparative *too* is part of that adjective's rendering; headed on *mighty*.
Rule 20: the explicit subject pronoun takes only its own English, *they*.
Comparative מִן → *for* after *too mighty*.
Rule 18: the suffix takes *me*.
אוּלַי → *peradventure*.
Rule 17: the finite verb takes its subject pronoun, auxiliary and lexical verb; headed on *prevail*.

Rule 55: the ASV supplies a subordinator for a clause whose Hebrew writes no conjunction at all (נַכֶּה stands asyndetically after אוּכַל), so the *that* answers to no morpheme. It is not folded into the verb, for the reason rule 51 gives about a supplied *also*.
Rule 17: subject pronoun, modal and lexical verb; headed on *smite*.
Rule 40: the בְּ whose object the ASV promotes to a bare direct object (*smite them*) keeps nothing.
Rule 18: the suffix takes the object pronoun *them*.

Rule 55: a coordinator and a subordinator written together at the recast clause's left edge are one rendering of the single waw — *and that* is named there explicitly — headed on the coordinator. Competing reading: head on *that*; the corpus heads a minority of such units that way.
Rule 17: *I may drive*, headed on the lexical verb.
Rule 18: the object suffix takes *them*.

Rule 24: מִן rendered by the multi-word preposition *out of*, headed on the token carrying the lexeme. Competing reading: take *out* as the particle of a phrasal *drive out* under rule 44 and leave the preposition a bare *of*; the corpus's *out of* treatment is preferred.
Rule 15: the article takes *the*.
אֶרֶץ → *land*.
כִּי → *for*.
Rule 17: *I know*, headed on the lexical verb.
Rule 16: the object marker is unrendered. The complementizer *that* is not one of the four families the marker can take — none of them is a clause subordinator — so it is not placed here.

Rule 55: the complementizer of *I know that ...* is supplied for a clause with no conjunction morpheme in it; the אֲשֶׁר following is the relative of the headless clause and already holds its own English.
Rule 46's first rider: where the Hebrew writes a relative of its own, that relative takes the supplied antecedent with it — *he whom* — headed on the relative word.
Rule 17: *thou blessest*.
Rule 20: the passive participle predicate takes the construction-supplied copula; headed on *blessed*.
Rule 14: the waw takes *and*.
Rule 46's first rider, as at s034: *he whom*, headed on the relative.
Rule 17: *thou cursest*.
Rule 17: the Hophal takes its passive auxiliary and lexical verb; headed on *cursed*.

review_notes: The waw of וְעַתָּה is aligned to *therefore* and עַתָּה to *now*; the alternative of giving *now therefore* whole to עַתָּה is named in that unit's note.

Two supplied subordinators are marked added under rule 55 (t022, t040): both stand over clauses the Hebrew leaves asyndetic. The third, t028, is contiguous with the waw's *and* and is placed with it as rule 55's *and that* pair.
מִן at s028 takes *out of* under rule 24 rather than leaving *out* with a phrasal *drive out*; the competing reading is recorded in the unit's note.
The demonstrative phrase הָעָם הַזֶּה has two article morphemes and one written determiner: הַזֶּה takes *this* under rule 41 and both articles are unrepresented under rule 47.
